system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: Imprinting control element
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Covers the ICE as a long-range regulatory element carrying a gametic imprint (usually DNA methylation, rarely H3K27me3), its role in imprinted clusters via a long non-coding RNA (Airn) or CTCF-dependent insulator (Igf2/H19), and the effect of deleting the element on each parental allele. Excludes imprinting disorders and plant imprinting.

ATOMS:
- MED-EPI-C05-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: The expression of the imprinted genes in an imprinted gene cluster is controlled by an imprinting control element (ICE).
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0108-s24] Fig. 5.3). The expression of the imprinted genes is controlled by an imprinting control element, also known as ICE.
- MED-EPI-C05-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: In most imprinted gene clusters, the imprinting control element (ICE) shows differential DNA methylation that was established in only one of the parents during gametogenesis (the gametic or primary imprint) and is then maintained exclusively on that allele throughout post-fertilization development.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0108-s25] In most imprinted gene clusters, the ICE shows differential DNA methylation,
    [MED-EPI-p0109-s01] which was established in only one of the parents during gametogenesis (gametic or primary imprint) and then maintained exclusively on this allele throughout post-fertilization development.
- MED-EPI-C05-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: The gametic imprint at an imprinting control element marks the maternal and paternal alleles differently in the respective zygote.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0109-s02] Thus, the gametic imprint marks the maternal or paternal alleles differently in the respective zygote.
- MED-EPI-C05-S2-01.r1 | S2
  ATOM: On the maternal chromosome, the imprinting control element (ICE) is unmethylated, allowing CTCF proteins to bind and form an insulator that blocks the enhancers from interacting with the promoters of Igf2 and Ins2, while the enhancers can interact with and activate H19.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0110-s12] On the maternal chromosome, the ICE is unmethylated, allowing CTCF proteins to bind and form an insulator that blocks the enhancers from interacting with the promoters of Igf2 and Ins2, while they can interact and activate H19.
- MED-EPI-C05-S2-02.r1 | S2
  ATOM: On the paternal chromosome, which lacks the gametic methylation imprint, the non-coding RNA Airn is expressed and silences Igf2r, Slc22a2, and Slc22a3 in cis.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0110-s11] On the paternal (Pat) chromosome, lacking the gametic methylation imprint, Airn is expressed and silences Igf2r, Slc22a2, and Slc22a3 in cis. b The genes of the Igf2 cluster are regulated by the same enhancers (E) distal to the H19 non-coding RNA gene (H19-NC).
- MED-EPI-C05-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: In the Igf2 cluster, if the imprinting control element is methylated, CTCF proteins cannot bind and the insulator does not form, so the enhancers can interact with the more distant promoters of the protein-coding genes Igf2 and Ins2.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0111-s02] If the ICE is methylated, CTCF proteins cannot bind and the insulator does not form, thus allowing the interaction of the enhancers with the more distant promoters of the protein-coding genes Igf2 and Ins2.
- MED-EPI-C05-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: Deletion of the imprinting control element on the allele that lacks the gametic imprinting mark leads to a switch, such that the expression of the imprinted genes in the cluster resembles that of the allele that normally carries the imprinting mark.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0109-s07] In contrast, deletion of the ICE on the allele without the gametic imprinting mark leads to a switch, such that the expression of the imprinted genes in the cluster now resembles that of the allele that is normally carrying the imprinting mark.
- MED-EPI-C05-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: Deletion of the imprinting control element usually has no effect on the expression of the genes on the allele that carries the imprinting mark.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0109-s06] Such a deletion has usually no effect on the expression of the genes on the allele carrying the imprinting mark.
- MED-EPI-C05-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: Although all initially studied imprinted gene clusters in the mouse carried a gametic imprint based on 5-methyl-cytosine, in macaques several imprinting control elements do not show differential DNA methylation in the gametes.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0109-s03] Initially, all studied imprinted gene clusters in the mouse carried a gametic imprint based on 5-methyl-cytosine (see book 7 Chap. 1 of Wutz), but this is not true in macaques where several ICEs do not show differential DNA methylation in the gametes.
